source.title: Going, going, gone: localizing abrupt offsets of moving objects.
source.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

confidence_rationale: The closest psychophysical match to MECH-501's core computational event: a forward-extrapolated position estimate that is pulled back toward the sensed position when an abrupt trajectory change produces a transient signal, with graded intermediate positions as transient strength and motion signal strength are traded off. Held at 0.55 because the paradigm is passive visual motion, not a committed action, and the 'reconstruction' is inferred from end-point reports rather than measured as a discontinuity in an internal estimate.
failure_signatures: The corrected percept is equally explained by a pure postdictive (no-extrapolation) account; the paper's two-process reading is favoured, not proven.
Passive object motion has no commitment, so evidence here cannot separate state-estimate correction from action decommitment, which is the distinction MECH-501 rests on.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Two competing position representations exist for moving objects: an extrapolated internal-model estimate that runs ahead of the sensory input, and a transient-driven signal elicited by sudden trajectory changes that corrects the forward-shifted estimate; weaker motion or stronger transients yield less forward displacement.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct analogue of ARC-129's forward-displaced s_hat(t+tau) and of MECH-501's backward pull toward s_hat(t) when a salient violation arrives. The graded trade-off (transient strength vs extrapolation strength) suggests the reconstruction should be magnitude-dependent rather than all-or-none, which is testable in REE.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Perceptual localisation of an external object, not the agent's own current-state estimate during a committed action. No consequence/value manipulation, so the 'sufficiently consequential' gate in the claim is untested; the violation here is sensory salience (onset/offset transient), not a prediction error weighted by consequence.
mapping.source_context: Three psychophysics experiments on localisation of moving objects that abruptly disappear, briefly disappear, or drop in contrast.

confidence_components.notes: Well-controlled psychophysics with a parametric manipulation; mapping is to the computational form only, not to action commitment.
